question: Does a literature-based soft speech-presence probability noise tracker recover from the upward-noise update blockage of hard energy VAD, and what speech-distortion or intelligibility cost accompanies recovery?
context: Follow-up motivated by previously observed hard-gate failure. The old six sentences are diagnostic/regression only. Eighteen additional sentences have not been used in previous selection/evaluation identified in the local experiment records. They belong to the same six NOIZEUS speakers, not independent new speakers. No claim of external preregistration.

frozen_settings.shared_TSNR: Existing 8 kHz, 200-sample Hann convention,80-sample hop,400FFT,initial0.10s PSD,DD0.99,gain floor0.15 and inherited gain constraint; same amplitude-preserving synthesis; update after enhancement; invalid/calibration/padded frames freeze all estimator states.

spp_matched.difference_from_spp_default: Only alpha_PSD=0.95, matching hard gate smoother; predeclared rate ablation, not another selection candidate.

frozen_settings.time_constant_caveat: Author example uses 16ms hop; coefficients are retained on this shared 10ms hop. This is an explicitly adapted tracker, not exact whole-system reproduction. The matched-alpha ablation isolates the PSD-smoothing coefficient effect within the same new framing.

primary_comparison: On new rise_6dB cases compare spp_default versus vad_selected in late four-band absolute log-power error. Also report comparison with fixed and spp_matched; no result-based choice of final method.
band_error: For one-sided FFT bins with DC/Nyquist weight1 and other bins weight2, use bands [0,500),[500,1000),[1000,2000),[2000,4000]. Sum estimate-before-update and known injected-noise periodogram over identical late frames within each band. Take mean over4bands of abs(10log10(sum_est/sum_noise)). This is finite-window realized-noise band-power agreement, not expected PSD truth. Report signed broadband bias and spectral NRMSE as secondary diagnostics; no per-bin logarithmic floor fitting.
spectral_NRMSE: L2 norm of difference between late time-mean one-sided estimated and injected-noise periodograms divided by L2 norm of time-mean injected-noise periodogram. Finite-window diagnostic; not a perceptual metric.
secondary_outcomes: Reference SNR and standard pystoi0.4.1 extended=False on unquantized samples801:N
Constant0/5/10/15dB andfall outcomes to expose degradation
Effective update weight mean over valid,speech-proxy and low-energy-proxy frames; binary update coverage is not compared between hard and soft methods
profile_construction: Same as previous controlled study: source residual=noisy-clean, shared first100ms, halfway through remaining samples start400-sample linear-in-dB ramp to+/-6dB, then hold. Constant source remixes must be exact. No normalization, delay fitting, clipping or reference input to enhancer.
aggregation: For constant benchmark average8noise/SNR cases within sentence. For each controlledprofile average2noises within sentence. Then average3new sentences within each known speaker; report6speaker points and grandmean. Also publish18sentence and allcase outcomes. Old6sentences separate. No population significance, confidenceinterval or unseen-speaker claim.

preselected_trace.reason: First unused sentence and same street/rise condition as earlier diagnostic; chosen before scoring.

checks: Frozen protocol and input/core hashes before execution
Source recurrence match on synthetic periodograms and independent Python reconstruction
SharedinitialPSD/prefix and fixed independence from VADthresholds
All252mixtures and1512methodrows retained, finite outputs and no STOI warnings
Rerun fresh extracted package selected example and verify savedresults
stopping_rule: Exactly252inputs and6methods, no parametersearch or redesign after viewing new outcomes. Implementation bugs may be corrected with recorded amendment and complete affected rerun; preserve run history. Publish improvements, degradations and inconclusive outcomes.
